text:
sara: FYI incoming escalation from ACME (acct acme-42). They say invoices were sent twice within ~30s and they got billed twice. They captured a snippet of our logs showing repeated tool invocations for `send_invoice`.

kevin: Can you paste the log lines and the request id? I can start a repro if we have the payload.

sara: request_id=rx-0a9f3b, customer provided the original request body (see below). They say they only clicked once.

sara: ```
POST /v1/generate 200
request_id=rx-0a9f3b
model: gpt-4o-infer
-> model returns function_call: {"name":"send_invoice","arguments":"{\\\"order_id\\\":\\\"ord-123\\\",\\\"amount\\\":199.00}"}
Invoke tool send_invoice (attempt 1) -> 200 OK
receipt: rcpt-xyz
ack to model sent
--- network hiccup between tool and ack (504 on our side)
Retry flow triggered by client-side/auto-retry -> re-invoke send_invoice (attempt 2) -> 200 OK
Event: fallback-to-non-tool path executed as well -> second email sent
```

mike: Quick question — is the fallback path supposed to run if the function_call completed successfully? Seems like we double-processed because the retry couldn't see the ack.

francesca: Looking at the runtime traces, the model_response callback sometimes arrives after we've already retried the function call. Our retry/fallback state machine currently treats missing ack as transient and will re-execute the selected action (tool or fallback). There's no global idempotency check keyed to (customer_id, function_name, normalized_args).

kevin: Do we have any dedupe that would catch `send_invoice` being run twice? Should have been caught at the payments service side but ACME uses our hosted tool adapter that forwards to their internal payment gateway — they said their gateway got two separate requests.

francesca: Right. Two problems: (1) retries re-run side-effectful tools because we only dedupe at the per-request RPC level, not per-function-call semantics; (2) fallback execution path (we try non-tool fallback when function call looks like failed) doesn't share the same execution id so it executes independently.

mike: Repro plan I can run locally: simulate a tool adapter that returns 200 for the actual call but the network between runtime and the adapter returns a 504 on the callback, causing the runtime to assume failure and retry. If the fallback path also executes a different codepath that calls `send_invoice` again, duplicate happens.

kevin: Minimal repro payload (customer reported):
```json
{
  "model": "gpt-4o-infer",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Please charge customer and send invoice for ord-123"}],
  "functions": [{"name":"send_invoice","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"order_id":{"type":"string"},"amount":{"type":"number"}},"required":["order_id","amount"]}}],
  "function_call": "auto"
}
```

francesca: Suggested mitigations: short-term: disable auto-fallback-to-non-tool for functions marked side-effectful (payments, emails) and surface an explicit error to the caller instead of trying an alternate path. Medium-term: add server-side idempotency using a hash of (customer_id, function_name, canonicalized_args) stored in a fast dedupe store with a TTL. Also propagate an execution_id into the tool adapter so adapters can reject replays.

mike: Also add an invariant: when a tool invocation returns success, we must not run a fallback action for the same logical intent. That requires atomic visibility of "tool success" to the fallback decision. Right now, ack race causes both branches.

kevin: For immediate mitigation for ACME: we can offer to refund duplicates and recommend they enable an external dedupe on their gateway, but ultimately we should patch the runtime.

francesca: Implementation notes:
- Add `execution_id` header to tool calls, persisted in runtime logs.
- When retrying, reuse same execution_id. Fallbacks must check recent execution_id results before running.
- Accept client-provided idempotency-key and make it canonical for function semantics.
- Update policy: mark `functions` with `side_effect: true` in model catalog; runtime refuses to auto-fallback for side-effect functions.

mike: Rough timeline: hotfix toggle to disable fallback for side-effectful functions (1 day). Follow-up PR for execution_id + dedupe store (2-3 days). Long-term: canonical arg hashing + admin config for function safety (1-2 sprints).

ops-bot: Incident created INC-2026-0427, priority P2, assigned to eng-runtime oncall.

kevin: I'll respond to customer with: "We've identified the likely cause (retry/fallback race) and are disabling auto-fallback for payment/email functions while we push a fix. We'll refund duplicate charges and follow up with timeline." :thumbsup:

francesca: One more caution — make sure billing dedupe logic also looks at `execution_id` before issuing invoice/charge to avoid double-billing if an external adapter misbehaves.

mike: I'll open the PR and ping here with a link. Thanks all.

sara: Thanks team — I've notified ACME of the temporary mitigation and refund plan.

kevin: (added) logs and traces uploaded to the incident ticket for anyone debugging: link: https://redwood.internal/incident/INC-2026-0427/traces
